description:
FOUND by the s509 review of s507p (Fable's table; reproducer ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/sb/sb.pl app-match 30000): a regex ANCHORED AT THE END of a string that grows by .= costs a scan from the string's START on every iteration, so append + match per iteration is QUADRATIC -- on main and on the s507p tree alike.  NOT the string-buffer work: a plain LEXICAL scalar (no buffer cell, no snapshot) shows it too.

Reproducer (s507p worktree: scratch/s507p/probes/appmatch2.pl SECTION N):
  my %h; my $m = 0; for my $i (1 .. $N) { $h{u} .= "line $i\n"; $m++ if $h{u} =~ /9\n\z/ } print "$m\n";

Measured 2026-10-06 08:22 (load ~8, wall incl. start-up); pcl = s507p tree bc276159, base = main fee16466:
  section                                N=10000   N=20000   perl N=20000
  match    ($h{u} =~ /9\n\z/)             2.17 s    8.34 s    0.03 s   (base 2.39 / 8.26)
  lexmatch (my $u =~ /9\n\z/)             1.34 s    5.54 s             (base 1.44 / 5.14)
  substr   (substr($h{u}, -2) eq "9\n")   0.28 s    0.84 s             (base 0.27 / 0.90)
THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: the same loop with substr(-2) in place of the match is ~10x faster, and the lexical spelling (no cell at all) is as quadratic as the element one -- so the cost is the regex engine, not the read of the string.  (The substr row's own residual growth is #2722, a snapshot per read of a buffer cell.)  Review table at 30000: perl 0.09 s, main 11.05, tree 10.80.

Suspect to measure first: perl starts an end-anchored match (\z, \Z, $) near the end of the string (its minlen / anchored-at-end check); PCL's engine tries every start position from 0.  Cheap test that confirms or kills it: time /9\n\z/ against /x\z/ (never matches) and against a one-shot match on a 1 MB string; if the one-shot is linear in the length and ~N/1 start positions are tried, the suspect is confirmed.
Filed only (s507p); owner: the regex engine.
subject: A regex anchored at the END (/X\z/) of a string growing by .= scans from the start on each match: append + match per iteration is quadratic (main and s507p alike; 8 s vs perl 0.03 s at 20k)
